To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
patients with metastatic renal cell cancer have improved survival with the use of targeted agents.
the use of multiple lines of treatment with targeted therapies is associated with improved survival in patients with metastatic clear cell RCC.
patients receiving sequential TKIs and/or mTOR inhibitors (including those receiving only a first-line therapy) have a better survival than those who do not receive targeted therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of new methods for the diagnosis, treatment and prognosis of cancer patients.
the development of a new therapeutic approach for patients with advanced RCC, which is based on the use of a combination of targeted drugs and the use of immunotherapy.
the treatment of metastatic renal cell carcinoma (RCC).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of targeted therapy in RCC has improved outcome in the past 10 years.
the availability of novel agents has improved the outcome of metastatic RCC in Switzerland, and that the use of sequential targeted therapy, TKI and mTORi is the key factor for improved survival.
in the era of targeted therapies for RCC the prognostic factors of tumor biology and treatment are of equal importance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the availability of novel systemic agents has improved the survival in RCC and that a more aggressive approach to the disease is warranted.
the outcome of RCC patients is improved when novel drugs are available and can be offered to the patients.
the use of novel targeted agents for RCC has improved the survival in patients with metastatic disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of surgical and medical interventions, including the use of multiple TKI and mTORi, has the potential to improve survival for patients with advanced renal cell carcinoma.
the use of targeted therapies has a positive effect on the outcome of patients with metastatic renal cell cancer.
a combination of targeted therapy with surgery and the availability of multiple lines of therapy is of utmost importance to improve the outcome in patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma.
